intended_application: An agent-assisted workflow that checks and improves internal enrollment and student-service dashboards before administrative review.
organization: A large private university with decentralized analytics teams and central privacy, security, and institutional-research offices.
industry_sector: Higher education administration and institutional analytics.
business_need: Reduce repeated dashboard-quality problems and help decentralized analysts apply consistent evidence and visualization checks.
users_stakeholders: Institutional researchers, school administrators, student-service teams, privacy and security staff, faculty leaders, and students represented in the data.
adoption_posture: Moderate and fast-follower. The university will experiment with mature components but expects privacy review, documented controls, and human approval.
capabilities_constraints: The university has data warehouses and BI tools but uneven local analytics skills, fragmented governance, limited integration capacity, and education-record privacy obligations.
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect dashboards can misallocate resources or misrepresent student outcomes. Exposure of student-level data would be consequential; internal draft revisions are otherwise reversible.
management_question: Should the university pilot agentic AI for dashboard quality assurance, and what design boundaries follow from the technology's creation history?
time_horizon: A six-month pilot before the next annual planning cycle.
additional_context: The pilot must use de-identified or role-authorized data, preserve lineage, and require institutional-research approval before dashboard release.
